metformin.dosage: Adults: 500 mg twice daily with meals, increasing to 850–1000 mg twice daily as tolerated. Maximum 2,550 mg/day in divided doses.
metformin.warnings: Do not use if you have kidney disease (eGFR <30), liver disease, or are having surgery/contrast imaging. Stop 48 hours before contrast dye procedures. Alcohol increases lactic acidosis risk.
metformin.storage: Store below 25°C, away from moisture and light.
metformin.pregnancy: Consult doctor — may be used with caution in gestational diabetes.

amoxicillin.dosage: Adults: 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours for 5–14 days depending on infection. Children: 25–45 mg/kg/day in divided doses. Always complete the full course.
amoxicillin.warnings: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin, cephalosporins, or any antibiotic. Do not stop taking early even if you feel better — incomplete courses promote resistance.
amoxicillin.storage: Store below 25°C. Reconstituted suspension: refrigerate and use within 14 days.
amoxicillin.pregnancy: Generally considered safe — consult your doctor.

uses: Mild to moderate pain (headache, toothache, muscle ache)
paracetamol.dosage: Adults: 500–1000 mg every 4–6 hours as needed. Maximum 4,000 mg (8 standard tablets) per 24 hours. Children: Follow weight-based dosing — see package insert.
side_effects: Liver damage (in overdose or with alcohol)
paracetamol.warnings: NEVER exceed 8 tablets (500 mg) per day. Many cold, flu, and combination medicines already contain paracetamol — check all labels to avoid double-dosing. Avoid alcohol. Reduce dose if you have liver disease.
paracetamol.pregnancy: Considered the safest painkiller in pregnancy — use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.

amlodipine.dosage: Adults: 5 mg once daily. May increase to 10 mg once daily after 7–14 days if needed. Take at the same time each day, with or without food. Elderly: Start at 2.5 mg.
amlodipine.warnings: Do not stop taking suddenly without doctor advice. Grapefruit and grapefruit juice can significantly increase blood levels — avoid during treatment. Use with caution in severe aortic stenosis or acute heart failure.
amlodipine.storage: Store below 30°C, protect from light and moisture.
amlodipine.pregnancy: Not recommended — discuss safer alternatives with your doctor.

ciprofloxacin.dosage: Adults: 250–750 mg every 12 hours for 3–14 days depending on infection type. Take with a full glass of water. Do not take with dairy products or calcium-fortified foods.
ciprofloxacin.warnings: Can cause tendon damage, especially the Achilles tendon — stop immediately if you have tendon pain. Avoid excessive sun exposure (causes sunburn). Not recommended for children under 18 or pregnant women. Can worsen myasthenia gravis.
ciprofloxacin.pregnancy: Avoid — not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

omeprazole.dosage: Adults: 20–40 mg once daily, 30–60 minutes before the first meal. Take for 4–8 weeks for ulcers; may be long-term for GERD. Do not crush or chew capsules.
side_effects: Long-term: Low magnesium, vitamin B12 deficiency, increased fracture risk
omeprazole.warnings: Long-term use (>1 year) may cause magnesium and vitamin B12 deficiency — get periodic blood tests. May mask symptoms of stomach cancer — report persistent symptoms. Increased risk of C. difficile diarrhoea.
omeprazole.storage: Store below 25°C, protect from light and moisture.
omeprazole.pregnancy: Generally considered safe — consult doctor for prolonged use.

uses: Diabetic nephropathy (kidney protection in type 2 diabetes)
Stroke prevention in hypertension with left ventricular hypertrophy
losartan.dosage: Adults: 50 mg once daily (starting dose). May increase to 100 mg once daily. Elderly or volume-depleted: Start at 25 mg. Can be taken with or without food.
side_effects: Dry cough (less common than ACE inhibitors)
losartan.warnings: Do not use during pregnancy — can cause serious fetal harm or death. Do not combine with ACE inhibitors or aliskiren (risk of kidney failure and high potassium). Monitor kidney function and potassium levels regularly.
losartan.pregnancy: CONTRAINDICATED — do not use during pregnancy.

ibuprofen.dosage: Adults: 200–400 mg every 4–6 hours with food or milk. Maximum 1,200 mg/day OTC; up to 3,200 mg/day under medical supervision. Children: Use weight-based paediatric formulations only.
side_effects: Stomach upset (common — always take with food)
ibuprofen.warnings: Always take with food or milk to protect the stomach. Avoid if you have a peptic ulcer, kidney disease, or heart failure. Increases risk of cardiovascular events with long-term use. Do not combine with other NSAIDs or aspirin. Avoid in the last trimester of pregnancy.
ibuprofen.pregnancy: Avoid in the third trimester — may cause premature closure of ductus arteriosus.

diclofenac.dosage: Adults: 75–150 mg daily in 2–3 divided doses with food. Maximum 150 mg/day. Topical gel: Apply 2–4 g to the affected area 3–4 times daily. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.
side_effects: Increased cardiovascular risk with long-term use
diclofenac.warnings: Diclofenac has a higher cardiovascular risk among NSAIDs — avoid if you have heart disease. Take with food to reduce stomach irritation. Avoid combining with other NSAIDs. Monitor liver function with prolonged use.

uses: Prevention of cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke)
atorvastatin.dosage: Adults: 10–20 mg once daily (starting dose). Dose may be adjusted to 10–80 mg once daily. Take at the same time daily, with or without food. Evening dosing maximises efficacy.
atorvastatin.warnings: Stop immediately and contact a doctor if you develop unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness — this could indicate rhabdomyolysis. Avoid grapefruit juice. Avoid alcohol. Report any unusual liver symptoms (jaundice, dark urine).
atorvastatin.storage: Store below 25°C, protect from light and moisture.
